question_english: In a relational database, a data structure that organizes all the information about a subject in the form of rows and columns.
technical_proof: A Table (relation) is the structure in a relational database that organizes all data about a subject into rows (records) and columns (fields).
explanation: A Table organizes subject-related data into rows and columns in a relational database.
trap_point: Record/Tuple refers to a single row within a table, not the entire row-and-column structure itself.
memory_trick: Whole grid of rows & columns = Table (not just one row = Record/Tuple).
revision_fact: Table = Relation; Row = Tuple/Record; Column = Attribute/Field.

question_english: What is another name for a row in a database?
technical_proof: A row in a relational database table is also referred to as a Record (or Tuple in formal relational terminology).
explanation: A row is also called a Record.
trap_point: Field/Column both refer to a vertical attribute, not a horizontal row — opposite concept.
memory_trick: Row = Record (horizontal); Column = Field (vertical).
revision_fact: Formal terms: Row=Tuple/Record, Column=Attribute/Field, Table=Relation.

question_english: Database transaction means-

options.text: डाटाबेस से डाटा उपार्जित करना / Acquiring data from database
डाटाबेस में डाटा लिखना / Writing data to the database
डाटाबेस में डाटा पढ़ना / Reading data in database
उपरोक्त सभी / All of the above

technical_proof: A database transaction is a logical unit of work that can consist of one or more operations — reading, writing, or otherwise accessing data — treated as a single all-or-nothing unit.
explanation: A transaction can involve reading, writing, or acquiring data, making 'All of the above' the correct broad definition.
trap_point: Students sometimes narrow 'transaction' to only mean 'writing data', but read operations within a unit of work also count as part of a transaction.
memory_trick: Transaction = Any unit-of-work operation (read/write/acquire), done atomically.
revision_fact: Transactions follow the ACID properties: Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability.
